title: The Sutta-Nipâta
attributionNote: The Sutta-Nipâta is an anthology of early Buddhist discourses, transmitted anonymously within the Khuddaka Nikâya. Individual suttas are presented as the Buddha's teaching but the collection as a whole is the work of the early community.
description: The Sutta-Nipâta gathers some of the oldest Buddhist poetry in five vaggas: the Uragavagga on the snake, the chariot and the farmer; the Kūlavagga of the charcoal-burner and the outcaste; the Mahāvagga with the discourse on friendliness and the going forth; the Aṭṭhakavagga on the abandonment of views; and the Pārāyanavagga of the questions of the brahmin youths. It is a primary witness to early Buddhist ethics and meditation.
historicalContext: The Sutta-Nipâta was translated by Viggo Fausböll for the Sacred Books of the East, volume 10 (1881), together with Müller's Dhammapada. Its archaic language and its treatment of brahmanical sacrifice make it central to the study of early Buddhism.
availabilityNote: Complete. All five vaggas of Fausböll's translation are streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time, one vagga per chapter. Each page is long because the printed edition prints a whole vagga at a time; the passage index follows its paragraphs. The volume's glossary and introduction are not part of the work.
